quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light. It tells drivers that left-turning traffic must wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: What must you do at a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before any crosswalk.

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see down all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop and block the emergency vehicle.
Get out of the way and give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal when it is safe for the emergency vehicle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the way and give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, give it a clear path. Move your vehicle to the side of the road if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is the speed limit for your vehicle?

options.text: The maximum speed limit posted.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than is reasonable and safe. Adjust your speed for the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting. Stay within posted speed limits.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Where can you not park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: What should you do after a collision?

options.text: Stop at or near the collision site. Move your car off the road if you can.
Stand or walk in traffic lanes while waiting for help.
Try to remove power lines if they are down in the road.
Move injured people, even if they are not in immediate danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at or near the collision site. Move your car off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a collision, stop at or near the site. If your car can be moved, get it off the roadway to a safe place.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a standard crossbuck sign. You should:

options.text: Approach the tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger signals it is safe, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is at the crossing, follow all their instructions.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Press your brakes firmly.
Release the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: To slow down on a slippery road, first release the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press your brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: Cannot exit the freeway.
Can either continue through the interchange or exit the freeway.
Can stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means the lane ends at an exit ramp. If you are in a lane with an "Exit only" sign, you can change lanes to continue on the highway, or you must exit.

questions.question: A vehicle buyer must transfer ownership and registration:

options.text: By the end of the year.
Before the license plate expires.
Within 15 days of the purchase date.
Within 60 days of the purchase date.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 15 days of the purchase date.
questions.explanation: You must transfer ownership within 15 days to avoid penalty fees. If a dealer sells the vehicle, the dealer is responsible for the transfer.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Leave the car and go look for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road and try to flag down other drivers.
Stay in your car where rescuers are most likely to find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car where rescuers are most likely to find you.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you remain in your vehicle. Walking outside in a snowstorm is also unsafe.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane well in advance. Do not slow down until after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself by passing slow drivers.
Following the car ahead at a close distance.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you deal with careless, reckless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead suddenly slows or stops.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead suddenly slows or stops.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front suddenly slows or stops, you will not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less harmful when drinking beer instead of wine.
Is less harmful when drinking wine instead of beer.
Is worst when drinking hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter—only how much alcohol you have consumed.

questions.question: To park legally on a street, your vehicle must be within:

options.text: Six inches of the curb.
12 inches of the curb.
18 inches of the curb.
24 inches of the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: You cannot park more than 12 inches away from the curb on a street.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Slow down without braking hard. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic before moving back onto the road.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances that use sirens or horns with flashing red or blue lights. Follow their loudspeaker directions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so wait until the way is completely clear before moving.

questions.question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
There are pedestrians crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.
